subject: amateur sommeliers
one_liner: A 4-millimeter cortical implant that streams certified tasting notes to your speech center 40 milliseconds before you can improvise.
brand_voice_notes: Grand cru wine label meets implantable-device spec sheet. Every sentence is written by a company that believes taste is a firmware problem and doubt is a pre-surgical condition. Never winks. Prices are quoted like allocations. Surgery is referred to as 'induction.' The word 'opinion' is always slightly suspect.

hero.h1: You are now correct about wine.
hero.sub: Palais is a 4mm cortical implant that delivers appellation-certified tasting notes directly to your speech center. Say 'crushed violets and graphite' with the conviction of someone who meant to.

features.title: Verbal Override
features.blurb: The implant intercepts your sentence 40 milliseconds before speech and replaces 'it's fruity?' with the certified descriptor. You hear yourself say it at the same time everyone else does. Most users describe this as a relief.

features.title: Optic Abstention
features.blurb: Blind tasting, enforced at the hardware level. Palais suspends your optic nerve at the table so the label cannot bias you. Vision resumes once you have committed to an opinion on record.

features.title: Reference Palate Sync
features.blurb: Nightly firmware aligns your taste receptors to a Master Sommelier in Lyon. Within six weeks you will be indistinguishable from him. Known side effects include hating everything you can afford.

testimonials.title: Regional Semi-Finalist, 2025 Okanagan Amateur Blind Tasting (Aromatics Division)

demo_screen_concept: The Decant Console: the implant's companion app mid-tasting. Left rail lists tonight's flight (four fake wines with vintages and a 'compatibility with your hardware' note). Center: a live cortical feed streaming detected compounds line by line, a large Conviction dial in percent, and a descriptor queue where certified adjectives arrive with certainty scores and the user approves or vetoes each before it is injected into the speech center. Approved descriptors assemble into a sentence preview; a gold 'SAY IT' button commits it (and logs it to the tasting record). A small red-labeled panic override reads 'revert to "it's nice"' and empties the queue. Selecting a wine and pressing 'sip' starts a new stream; conviction rises with approvals and collapses on panic.

design_direction.style: Engraved grand-cru appellation label crossed with an implantable-device spec sheet, cellar-dark claret mode. The page is staged as the release site of a heavily funded neurotechnology company that has decided taste is a firmware problem and sells elective brain surgery with the visual language of a Burgundy allocation letter. A near-black claret ground (#140A0D) runs the whole page with no gradient washes and no glow; structure comes from wine-label print chrome: fine double-rule frames (two 1px parchment-alpha lines 3px apart) boxing every panel, section headings set as centered small-caps banderoles between short horizontal rules, and roman-numeral section numbering (I. THE DEVICE, II. THE TIERS), so the page reads as a label engraved at estate scale rather than a website. Panels are label stock: flat fills one shade lighter than the ground (#1D1014), the double-rule frame in place of borders, 2px near-square radii, no shadows, no glass, no blur, no clay; depth comes entirely from print structure and the rationed metals. The core motif is the appellation seal: a circular SVG stamp reading CORTICALLY CERTIFIED around a 4mm implant glyph, rendered in gold line-work, sitting in the hero like an AOC mark, shrinking into list bullets and tier badges, and appearing once per section as a corner hallmark. One gold leaf (#C79A3B) carries the wordmark, every primary CTA, the seal, and one italicized word per headline; one rationed surgical mint (#6FD3B6) is reserved strictly for live clinical telemetry (the implant status dot, conviction readouts, compound feeds) so the medical device keeps interrupting the wine label, and appears nowhere else. Bodoni Moda sets the wordmark and headlines in high-contrast didone with estate-bottled confidence; Jost carries plain, faintly regulatory body copy. Every figure that pretends to be device telemetry (conviction percentages, descriptor counts, firmware versions, tier prices) is set in Courier Prime with tabular figures inside thin-ruled parchment wells, so it reads like the lot code stamped on the back label, not marketing. Motion is cellar-restrained: the seal rotates once slowly on load (12s, then stops), double rules draw outward from center on scroll, the mint status dot pulses on a 4s cycle, CTAs brighten their gold on hover and depress 1px on press, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No light mode, no glass, no blur panels, no neon glow, no clay, no bento lattice, no brutalist offset shadows, no marketplace cards, no condensed athletic type, no sign-painter rounding, no emoji. Reads like a company that files your palate under 'peripheral hardware' and considers hesitation a recall event.
design_direction.archetype: Premium DTC hardware launch page staged as a vintage release: hero as label front, device spec strip, features as numbered label clauses, testimonials as cellar notes with headshots, pricing as allocation tiers, footer as back-label fine print.
design_direction.motion_vocab: One slow ceremonial seal rotation on load; rules that draw outward; a 4s mint telemetry pulse; 1px CTA depress; 6px section fade-ups with 40ms stagger; everything behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Centered label composition: small-caps eyebrow (ESTATE-IMPLANTED · LOT 4MM-26), the gold appellation seal above the headline, Bodoni Moda headline at label scale with 'correct' in gold italic, Jost sub-copy at measure, one gold CTA and one ghost secondary ('Read the surgical terms'), and a thin-ruled telemetry strip underneath streaming compound names in Courier Prime with the mint status dot.
